question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & 4 & -5 \\ -5 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

 
The matrix $A$ has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=9.$
Find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{-1}AP.$
question.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  Notice that we are already given the eigenvalues of the matrix: 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=1,\,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=9.$

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ Applying our usual method, we get the following.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & 5 & -5 \\ -5 & -5 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1)I)x=0$ gives us the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-1I & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -5 & -5 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-1I)x=0$ gives us the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -5 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{3}=9,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-9I & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & -5 & -5 \\ -5 & -5 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-9I)x=0$ gives us the eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
